horizon.boost.title: Horizon Boost
horizon.boost.thermal.unavailable: Thermal state: not reported by this device
horizon.boost.preset.performance.desc: 8 chunks, no clouds, minimal particles, rain within 3 blocks with half its columns and splashes, solid leaves. The most frames and the least heat.
horizon.boost.preset.balanced.desc: 12 chunks, fast clouds, decreased particles, a 5-block rain radius. Close to vanilla's look at a lower cost.
horizon.boost.preset.quality.desc: 16 chunks, and vanilla's look for everything else. The full picture, at the full cost.
horizon.boost.preset.custom.desc: Your own choices. Changing any quality setting switches to this.
horizon.boost.note.smart: Always on: only animated textures visible on screen are updated, and rain splashes and texture animations never pause the game's ticks.
horizon.boost.knob.render_distance.desc: How many chunks around you are drawn in full detail. The largest cost: GPU time and memory grow with its square.
horizon.boost.knob.entity_distance.desc: How far mobs and items are drawn, as a share of the normal range. Lower saves CPU and GPU time in busy places.
horizon.boost.knob.particles.desc: How many particles effects spawn (smoke, splashes, crits). Medium cost in fights, near fire and in rain.
horizon.boost.knob.clouds.desc: 3D clouds, flat clouds or none. 3D clouds cost a little more GPU time than flat ones.
horizon.boost.knob.weather.desc: Draws falling rain and snow, their splashes and the rain sound. Off removes the whole weather cost but also what it looks like.
horizon.boost.knob.weather_radius.desc: How far around you rain and snow fall (vanilla's Weather Radius: 10 is Fancy, 5 is Fast). Rain's GPU cost grows with this distance.
horizon.boost.knob.weather_density.desc: The share of rain and snow columns drawn. Half the columns roughly halves rain's GPU time; the rain looks sparser.
horizon.boost.knob.rain_splashes.desc: Splash particles where rain lands. Fewer save CPU time on particles; the rain sound stays.
horizon.boost.knob.leaves.desc: Leaves you can see through, as in vanilla's Fancy leaves. Off draws them solid, which is faster in forests.
horizon.boost.knob.biome_blend.desc: Blends grass, foliage and water colours across biome borders. Costs chunk building time only, not frame time.
horizon.boost.knob.mipmaps.desc: Smaller copies of block textures for distant terrain: less shimmer. Costs a little texture memory, no frame time.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_all.desc: Animates water, lava, fire, portals and other moving block textures. Off freezes all of them and saves a little GPU time every tick.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_water.desc: Moving water surfaces, still and flowing. Off holds the current frame.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_lava.desc: Moving lava surfaces, still and flowing. Off holds the current frame.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_fire.desc: Flickering fire, soul fire and campfire flames. Off holds the current frame.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_portal.desc: The swirling purple of nether portals. Off holds the current frame.
horizon.boost.knob.animate_other.desc: Every other animated block: sea lanterns, prismarine, magma, kelp, command blocks and more. Off holds their current frames.
horizon.boost.knob.sky.desc: Draws the sky colour, sun, moon and stars. Off shows only the fog colour and saves a little GPU time.
horizon.boost.knob.stars.desc: The stars at night. Costs almost nothing.
horizon.boost.knob.sun_moon.desc: The sun and the moon in the sky. Costs almost nothing.
horizon.boost.knob.fog.desc: Distance fog that hides the edge of the loaded world. Off shows the edge; water, lava and darkness keep their fog. No cost either way.
horizon.boost.knob.fog_start.desc: Where the edge fog begins, as a share of the render distance. Vanilla starts it in the last tenth; lower values hide chunk loading sooner. No cost.
horizon.boost.knob.vignette.desc: Darkens the screen's edges. One full-screen layer: off saves a little GPU fill time.
horizon.boost.knob.entity_shadows.desc: Round shadows under mobs and items. Low cost, more where many mobs gather.
horizon.boost.knob.max_fps.desc: The most frames per second the game draws. A lower cap saves battery and heat; 60 is smooth on most phones.
horizon.boost.knob.resolution_scale.desc: World pixels per screen pixel; menus stay sharp. 70% draws about half the pixels: the biggest GPU saving, a softer picture.
horizon.boost.knob.chunk_updates.desc: Built chunk sections sent to the GPU per frame. Lower keeps frames smoother while terrain loads; new terrain appears more slowly.
horizon.boost.knob.workers.desc: Threads that generate, light and build chunks. Fewer threads heat the phone less but load terrain more slowly. Applies at the next start.
horizon.boost.knob.thermal.desc: When Android reports the phone heating up, lowers the frame cap first, then chunk uploads, then the render scale; restores them after it has cooled for 30 seconds. Changes nothing while the phone is cool.
horizon.boost.knob.thermal_readout.desc: Adds the thermal state and any heat limit to the performance overlay. No cost.
horizon.boost.knob.overlay.desc: Frame rate and frame, CPU and GPU times in a corner, with an optional graph. Costs almost nothing.
horizon.boost.knob.battery_mode.desc: At most 60 FPS in a world and 30 in menus, and half the chunk threads. Saves power and heat; what frames show stays the same.
